C-HISTORICAL-ASSERTION-REVIEW-1-C6AA9BFE.Summary: Draw the boundary by purpose and dependency, not by file version. Archives are historical metadata that may predate current requirements; an unchanged version number cannot establish that today's requirements applied at the historical checkpoint. Current obligations stay strict — root context, graph, verification, active change bundles, current execution/approval/apply, and the selected current close. Unrelated archived change bundles stop being current-validation inputs: they produce no lint error and no lint warning (so `--fail-on warnings` cannot be blocked by history), they grant no fabricated credit, and they are read field-by-field through a historical reader that reports `unavailable` — with a nonempty reason and no scope payload — distinctly from `absent`, `null`, and `declared-none`. Selection is not execution: `change show`, a historical `context --change`, and an explicit historical `review` may read a record for learning without making its old `MustExist` claims requirements on today's filesystem. The historical integrity audits stay honest — the F286 attempt-pair audit and the F16 same-ID relocation / foreign-ID detection remain available as information, separated from current-work gate compliance — and the selected current close keeps evaluating required `CloseEvidence` and refuses a `pass` on failed, incomplete, identity-mismatched, or unavailable evidence, including the measured empty-evaluation hole. Repair the T-005 warning guard and the `ngrace-plan` rule-19 rationale with evidence that fails on an unchanged misleading paragraph, and overturn the whole-archive malformed-refusal contract explicitly.

Goals.Goal: Current obligations stay strict and unchanged: root context, graph, verification, and active change bundles keep their current errors and severities, driven through their real surfaces (grammar and review); a current execution, approval, or apply transition is unaffected by history.

Project-wide lint, index, status, and context are not blocked by, and emit no error or warning for, an unrelated archived change bundle — whether it declares a different version, omits a current-only required section under the current version, or does not parse. Whole-project lint is clean at error and warning severity with such a record present.

A historical read reports supported fields and distinguishes `unavailable` from `absent`, `null`, and `declared-none`; the exact `ChangeDurableScope` and `ChangeView.observedWriteScope` union members, their selection rules, and both JSON and text output are bound and tested with known-field, unknown-field, absent-field, and explicit-`None` controls.

The historical integrity audits remain available and honest: the F286 attempt-pair audit and the F16 same-ID relocation / foreign-ID detection still run and still report, but their historical results are informational and do not block current work or re-enter lint.

The selected current close stays strict after its own archive arrival: every required `CloseEvidence` command is evaluated, a failed or incomplete command refuses `pass`, and a missing or malformed `AcceptanceCriteria` container, wrong wrapper identity, unparsable spec, or unavailable applied-status evidence refuses `pass` instead of recording an empty evaluation.

The T-005 warning guard observes the finding independently of unrelated error counts with controlled warning-only exit 0 and current-error exit 1; and the `ngrace-plan` rule-19 rationale, its packaged mirror, the skill-byte footprint pin, and the README footprint row and review note are corrected together, with an unchanged misleading paragraph failing the evidence even when byte totals match.

Constraints.Constraint: Ceremony tier T3 (architectural), **proposed, not ratified**: this is a redesign of the archive-validation, reader, and close-evidence boundary across five modules, and it changes user-visible lint, review, and `change show` output. The authority may reduce the tier; the tier changes section depth only, never whether gates run.

**Purpose and dependency boundary.** Every consumer is classified by purpose. *Current obligations*: project-wide lint/index/status/context and every current transition (`gate approve`, `gate verdict`, `gate apply`, `ngrace apply`, `gate archive`) — strict, current-format, current-filesystem. *Historical learning*: `change show`, `context --change` on an archived bundle, and an explicit historical `review` — field-level reads, no current conformance claim, no filesystem requirement from old `MustExist`. *Historical integrity audit*: the F286 attempt-pair audit and the F16 relocation/foreign-ID detection — informational, separated from gate compliance. A consumer never acquires current obligations merely because it selected a record; in particular a bare `review --change C-ID` is a historical audit, not a close. The close seam is `recordReviewVerdict` / `evaluateCloseEvidenceChildren`, the callers of the selected `gate verdict`.

**Field/response contract for the historical view (binding).** `ChangeDurableScope` gains a fourth member `{ state: "unavailable"; reason: string }` and `ChangeView.observedWriteScope` becomes `ChangeScopeSummary | { state: "unavailable"; reason: string } | null`. In both, the unavailable member carries a **nonempty** `reason` and **no** scope payload — never empty files/globs, never called empty. Historical section states are distinguished explicitly: `carried`/summary when the section is present and interpretable, `declared-none` for an explicit `<None />`, `absent`/`null` when the section is genuinely not present. Selection rules: (a) a *supported historical field shape* — the section parses into the known elements — yields `carried`/summary regardless of the record's `graceVersion`; a version difference alone is never an unavailable-field test; (b) a *genuine field absence* yields `absent`/`null`; (c) an explicit `None` yields the existing shape (durable `declared-none`, observed summary with empty arrays); (d) an *uninterpretable field shape* — the section is present but its shape is not one the reader recognizes, expressed by the existing `scope.invalid-durable-shape` / `scope.invalid-observed-shape` / `scope.invalid-context-artifact` issues — yields `unavailable` with the reason. `formatChangeText` (`src/query/render.ts:196-236`) and `formatDurableScope` must report the unavailable state and its reason distinctly from absent/declared-none; JSON emission (`src/grace-change.ts:118`) carries the exact union member.

**Required-field response for historical context (binding).** `context --task T-* --change C-ID` against an archived bundle has one concrete contract: an unparsable plan or spec refuses with `GraceCommandError("invalid-project", "Unreadable plan|spec at …")` carrying **no** `issues` (the existing `src/grace-context.ts:443-455,529-533` shape); a readable plan whose required task is absent or whose `ImplementationPlan` shape is unrecognized refuses with the existing `not-found` / `Task T-* not found in C-ID`; a readable spec whose `Satisfies` target has no body yields the existing per-criterion `{ verdict: "unable-to-determine", reason }` absence, never a silent empty. No current-filesystem `MustExist` requirement is imposed and no future migration is required to read the slice. The `change show` unparsable-spec/plan refusal keeps `project.unreadable-artifact` (`src/query/change.ts:148-164`); the two error shapes stay distinct.

**Selected-close evidence contract (binding), closing every empty-evaluation variant.** For a bundle resolved under `archive/`, `gate verdict --outcome pass` refuses unless the spec is readable, uses the `NgraceChangeSpec` root, carries exactly one direct `C-*` wrapper whose tag equals the bundle id, declares `status="applied"`, and has a present, interpretable `AcceptanceCriteria` container with at least one valid `AC-*` criterion. Every `CloseEvidence` child with at least one non-empty `Command` executes through the shell; a non-zero command refuses `pass` with the existing refusal. A `CloseEvidence` child that is incomplete (no `Command`, or an empty `Command`) refuses `pass` — `isCompleteCloseEvidence` (`src/artifact/grammar.ts:2199-2201`) currently drops such children silently, so rejecting only whole-XML parse failure is not enough. A missing/malformed/uninterpretable `AcceptanceCriteria` container, a wrong or missing wrapper identity, an unparsable spec, and unavailable applied-status evidence all refuse `pass`, and none may fall through to the pre-archive empty-return path. A readable applied wrapper with a valid container and genuinely no `CloseEvidence` criterion is the legitimate zero-command case and still permits `pass`. For the active (pre-archive) close the empty-return path is preserved. The verdict vocabulary (`pass | fail | unable-to-determine`) is unchanged.

**Close instruments substantiate their promises.** `AC-CURRENT-OBLIGATIONS-STRICT` drives the actual review surface (`runReview` / real `ngrace review`) for the active `MustExist` error, not only the grammar validator. `AC-SKILL-FOOTPRINT` asserts the corrected rule-19 meaning and the bounded README review note with a discriminating content assertion — the old clause absent, the new treatment present — so an unchanged misleading paragraph with matching byte totals fails; the numeric `total`/`totalBytes` pins and the README measurement relation remain. No full suite is duplicated and no implementation-mirroring test is added; the `examples/` byte freeze stays separate from the `bun run validate:examples` behavior check.

**Forced production set (9).** `src/artifact/grammar.ts` and `src/artifact/scope.ts` (`M-GRAMMAR`): exclude archived change bundles from current validation, and grant applied scope credit only from readable scope fields. `src/query/core.ts`, `src/query/change.ts`, and `src/query/render.ts` (`M-QUERY`): operational validation blocks on active plans only; the historical view carries the unavailable union and its selection rules; text rendering handles the unavailable member. `src/lint/core.ts` (`M-LINT-CORE`): archived plans leave current assertion lint. `src/review/core.ts` and `src/review/catalog.ts` (`M-REVIEW`): the archived-`MustExist` audit and its `info` guide. `src/gates/ledger.ts` (`M-GATES`): the selected-close evidence contract. `src/grace-context.ts` was re-checked and is **not** forced: its existing refusal and `unable-to-determine` shapes are the bound historical-context contract, and the unrelated-malformed-archive fix lives in grammar/query. Any further required write is reported for ratification before it is added.

**Forced non-source set (4).** `skills/ngrace/ngrace-plan/SKILL.md` and its packaged mirror `plugins/ngrace/skills/ngrace/ngrace-plan/SKILL.md` are corrected: rule 19's rationale for carrying a read-only `.ngrace/scratch` in a faithful post-close copy no longer claims that without it `review.confidently-wrong` fires on archived plans — under this design an archived plan's `MustExist` is a `review.historical-path-absent` historical notice, and the copy is carried so the selected close and any historical audit read the same tree. The two copies stay byte-identical. `src/test-support/token-accounting.test.ts` pins the re-measured skill-text `total`/`totalBytes` **and** asserts the corrected rule-19 meaning; `README.md`'s footprint row is updated to the same re-measured string and gains a bounded `ngrace review` note that archived history is audited as historical information. This is a user-visible documentation change and is not justified by claiming immutability.

**Forced test set (9).** `src/artifact/grammar.test.ts`, `src/artifact/scope.test.ts`, `src/query/change.test.ts`, `src/grace-query.test.ts`, `src/grace-context.test.ts`, `src/lint/core.test.ts`, `src/review/core.test.ts`, `src/verification/localize.test.ts`, and `src/gates/core.test.ts`. `src/query/change.test.ts:123-125` accesses `.files`/`.globs` on a non-null-asserted observed scope and is forced to narrow under the new union; the whole `src/**/*.ts` tsconfig includes it. The matrix was re-derived by grepping the whole `src/` and `scripts/` test and teaching-pin population for every moved behavior, the `ChangeView` symbol search, each pinned count, and the skill/README footprint. `src/grace-status.ts` and `src/grace-status.test.ts` are checked and not forced because status consumes the tolerant lint. The plan re-confirms the population before ratification.

**No historical lint output.** Archived change bundles are not current-validation inputs, so their grammar, section, status, and assertion issues are neither errors nor warnings in the lint result. A `--fail-on warnings` run over a project carrying a malformed, version-changed, or current-only-section-missing archived bundle exits 0. The corruption is not silently erased: a consumer that selects the record surfaces it — `change show` reports `project.unreadable-artifact` for an unparsable record, and `context --change` refuses with `Unreadable plan|spec at …`.

**Historical audit severities.** The archived-`MustExist` audit emits `review.historical-path-absent` at `info` with the F16 relocation/foreign-ID distinctions in its message (present under the same-ID archive alias is silent; missing under both aliases and a foreign-id substitution are reported as historical notices). It never emits `review.confidently-wrong`, and it does not fail a project-wide `review` (which exits nonzero only on errors). Active plans keep `review.confidently-wrong` / `must-exist-missing`, including the same-ID alias resolution, missing-both refusal, and foreign-ID refusal. The F286 attempt-pair audit is unchanged at `warning` and its abandoned-bundle exemption is not widened.

**Authorized API change and its consequences.** The `ChangeView` union widening above is the only authorized API change. Consequences, all in the write scope: `src/query/render.ts` narrows and renders the unavailable member; `src/query/change.test.ts` narrows its field accesses and gains the known/unknown/absent/None fixtures; JSON consumers receive the exact member and need no change. No other error-shape change is authorized.

**Prior-ruling overturns, with counterweights.** (a) The `C-ARCHIVE-CORPUS-BASELINE-2` / `C-PER-BUNDLE-READERS-1-58BB7AB1` regression at `src/grace-context.test.ts:455` requires an **unrelated** malformed archived `spec.xml` to refuse the whole context slice; that is overturned — the unrelated archive is not a current-validation input and the slice returns its base output, while the corruption stays observable through the selected reader's refusal. A **selected** malformed active or archived change still refuses, and the regression is updated two-sided. (b) The F16 counterweight (`C-REPORT-HONESTY/spec.xml:232-242`) made an archived plan's missing-both-alias and foreign-ID `MustExist` errors; under this design those are historical audit notices, because a review of archived history is not a current obligation, while active plans keep the error. The relocation and foreign-ID **detection** is retained and reported. (c) The whole-archive grammar coupling is removed; no version dispatcher is added and no `NGRACE_ARTIFACT_VERSION` bump is required, because no current working state becomes an error. No historical artifact byte is rewritten.

`bun run ngrace lint --path . --assertions current` after this draft is the pre-implementation active-baseline check, never target or final evidence. The full CI-equivalent `bun run validate:ci` runs at plan `--assertions final --run-commands` and again as a post-archive close-bound criterion.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No historical grammar implementation, version dispatcher, or migration tooling. Archives are read as metadata; an uninterpretable field is `unavailable`, never a fabricated interpretation. Owner: a future migration change only if a real historical format is produced.
No rewrite, move, deletion, or semantic reinterpretation of any archived artifact. Owner: unchanged; archives are immutable.
No new lint code and no archive lint warning: history does not enter the lint result. Owner: unchanged; the current lint catalog is not extended.
No suppression of the F286 or F16 audits, no detector change, and no CLI exit-semantics change. Owner: unchanged; the audits stay live and warnings still exit 0.

No change to current obligations: active assertions, current-source verification, and current transitions keep their strictness. Owner: unchanged; strictness is retained where an obligation is current.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CURRENT-OBLIGATIONS-STRICT:
Root context, graph, verification, and active change bundles keep their current validation errors and severities. The actual review surface is driven, not only the grammar validator: an active plan's present-absence `MustExist` still raises `review.confidently-wrong` / `must-exist-missing` through `runReview` / the real `ngrace review`, including the corr-171 same-ID alias resolution (silent when present), missing-both refusal (error), and foreign-ID refusal (error); and a malformed active artifact still refuses through the grammar validator. A test selectable by `-t "current obligations stay strict"` in `src/review/core.test.ts` drives the review half; a test selectable by `-t "active stays strict"` in `src/artifact/grammar.test.ts` drives the grammar half.
bun test --timeout=0 src/review/core.test.ts -t "current obligations stay strict" bun test --timeout=0 src/artifact/grammar.test.ts -t "active stays strict"
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-HISTORICAL-NOT-CURRENT-OBLIGATIONS:
An unrelated archived change bundle produces no lint error and no lint warning in each of three cases: (a) its `graceVersion` differs from the installed version; (b) it parses with the installed version but omits a current-only required section such as `Summary`; and (c) it does not parse. In all three, `bun run ./src/grace.ts lint --path . --fail-on warnings` exits 0 with an empty error and warning count; `loadGraceArtifactIndex`, `ngrace status`, and `ngrace context` succeed; and exact restoration of the archived bytes restores the exact base output. The probe mutates a physical throwaway copy, never the production archive. A test selectable by `-t "archived history is not a current obligation"` carries this assertion.
bun test --timeout=0 src/artifact/grammar.test.ts -t "archived history is not a current obligation"
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-HISTORICAL-VIEW-CONTRACT:
The `ChangeView` union is exactly `ChangeDurableScope = carried | declared-none | absent | { state: "unavailable"; reason: string }` and `observedWriteScope = ChangeScopeSummary | { state: "unavailable"; reason: string } | null`, with a nonempty reason and no scope payload on the unavailable member. Real `ngrace change show` JSON emits the exact union member and text reports the unavailable state and reason distinctly from absent/declared-none, for the four controls: (1) a known-field fixture (durable `carried`, observed summary) regardless of a differing `graceVersion`; (2) an explicit `<None />` (durable `declared-none`, observed empty summary — not unavailable); (3) a genuine absent section (durable `absent`, observed `null`); (4) an uninterpretable field shape (durable or observed `unavailable` with a nonempty reason — not empty, not absent). A version difference alone is never an unavailable-field test. A test selectable by `-t "historical view unavailable contract"` drives both formats.
bun test --timeout=0 src/query/change.test.ts -t "historical view unavailable contract"
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-HISTORICAL-CONTEXT:
`ngrace context --task T-* --change C-ID` against an archived bundle reads supported plan and spec fields, imposes no current-filesystem `MustExist` requirement, and does not require a future migration merely to read the slice. An unparsable plan or spec refuses with `invalid-project` / `Unreadable plan|spec at …` and **no** `issues`; a readable plan whose required task is absent or whose `ImplementationPlan` shape is unrecognized refuses with `not-found` / `Task T-* not found in C-ID`; a readable spec whose `Satisfies` target has no body yields the per-criterion `{ verdict: "unable-to-determine", reason }` absence, never a silent empty. A test selectable by `-t "historical context reads supported fields"` carries this assertion.
bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-context.test.ts -t "historical context reads supported fields"
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-NO-FABRICATED-CREDIT:
Applied-scope credit is derived only from readable scope fields of an applied archived bundle. A bundle whose plan is unparsable, or whose durable or observed scope fields are unavailable, grants no credit, and the lack of credit is distinguishable from a legitimate `declared-none`/empty scope. A readable archived bundle's applied scope still explains drift exactly as today. A test selectable by `-t "unreadable history grants no credit"` carries this assertion.
bun test --timeout=0 src/artifact/scope.test.ts -t "unreadable history grants no credit"
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REVIEW-ARCHIVED-AUDIT:
An archived plan's missing `MustExist` yields `review.historical-path-absent` at severity `info` — never `review.confidently-wrong` — with the same-ID archive alias present silent, and with the missing-both-alias and foreign-id cases reported as historical notices that name the target and state current absence while leaving archive-time presence unevaluated (the message or explanation contains `archive-time` and `unevaluated`). A project-wide `ngrace review` exits 0 with these notices present, and `--severity info` surfaces them. Active plans keep `review.confidently-wrong` / `must-exist-missing` per `AC-CURRENT-OBLIGATIONS-STRICT`. A test selectable by `-t "archived existence claim is a historical audit"` carries this assertion.
bun test --timeout=0 src/review/core.test.ts -t "archived existence claim is a historical audit"
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-PRESERVED-AUDITS:
The F286 attempt-pair audit still reddens an `applied` archived bundle at `warning` and still exempts an abandoned `superseded`/`rejected`/`cancelled` bundle; the unemitted verification `Marker` check still fires; the scope, `WriteEvidence`-scope, verdict, approval, and close-evidence audits keep their codes, severities, and finding IDs; and retirement still consumes archive directory names without a new decoder. No historical finding is silently erased. A test selectable by `-t "historical integrity audits preserved"` carries the core half.
bun test --timeout=0 src/review/core.test.ts -t "historical integrity audits preserved"
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-SELECTED-CLOSE-STRICT:
For the selected **archived** bundle, `gate verdict --outcome pass` refuses unless the spec is readable, uses the `NgraceChangeSpec` root, has exactly one direct `C-*` wrapper whose tag equals the bundle id, declares `status="applied"`, and has a present, interpretable `AcceptanceCriteria` container with at least one valid `AC-*` criterion. A readable applied wrapper with a valid container and genuinely no `CloseEvidence` criterion still permits `pass`, and the active pre-archive empty-return path is preserved. C-HISTORICAL-ASSERTION-REVIEW-1-C6AA9BFE.Problem:
The queue's “Historical archive compatibility: immediate derivation and defect repair” entry (`docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/grace-implementation-queue.md`) records the maintainer's instruction to derive and repair confirmed defects promptly. The maintainer's policy is that archives are historical metadata that may predate current requirements, and that an unchanged version number cannot establish that today's requirements applied at the historical checkpoint. “No blanket exemptions” protects current obligations and meaningful integrity evidence; it does not turn unrelated historical records into current obligations.
**The measured coupling.** All 165 archived bundles (322 spec+plan roots) declare `graceVersion="1.0"`. On a physical throwaway copy of the checkout, the root lint is 0 errors; each of three independent mutations of one **unrelated** archived bundle makes it fail while the mutation is present and returns to 0 when the exact bytes are restored: (a) changing the spec's `graceVersion` to `0.9` yields `artifact.unsupported-grace-version`; (b) removing the required `Summary` section while keeping `1.0` yields `change.spec-missing-section`; (c) malformed XML yields four errors — `change.applied-plan-missing` and three `xml.parse`. Because `validateNgraceProject` (`src/artifact/grammar.ts:1329-1356`) walks the archive and `loadGraceArtifactIndex` (`src/query/core.ts:129-151`) throws on any error, `ngrace status`, `ngrace context`, and the query index all fail because of a record the current work did not select. Case (b) is why the version number cannot be the boundary: a 1.0 archive that predates a later required section is held to a requirement that did not exist at its checkpoint.
**The filesystem coupling.** `detectConfidentlyWrong` (`src/review/core.ts:504-558`) reads every archived plan's `MustExist` against the current filesystem and reports `review.confidently-wrong` / `must-exist-missing`. Measured 2026-10-02: three such errors on `test-metrics.json` — two in `C-MINT-BASELINE-CONTROL-3-F04434E4/plan.xml` (baseline and target) and one in `C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-4-F173437E/plan.xml` (target) — whose files coexisted with their applied archived plans at the historical checkpoints (`06996d6`, `a104166`) and were later retired by the approved `C-DECLARATION-GUARD-RETIRE-1-C69B6AB6`; a tracked-only copy adds eleven more across eight applied archived plans for the ignored `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md`. The current filesystem cannot decide a historical claim. Selection is not execution: a `change show` or historical `review --change` of one of these records is learning, not a current close.
**The measured close-evaluation hole.** An authority/Luna empirical probe on a disposable physical copy found that the public `gate verdict --outcome pass` refused an original applied spec with `CloseEvidence Command exited non-zero; refuse to record outcome pass.`; after only the selected fixture spec became malformed, the same acknowledged verdict command recorded `pass` (exit 0), because `evaluateCloseEvidenceChildren` (`src/gates/ledger.ts:546-570`) returns an empty set when the spec has no parseable root. The same probe wrote and then restored the production ledger through a hardlinked fixture; the authority independently verified exact restoration to HEAD and archive diff exit 0. That unsafe method is not repeated here, and the probe attribution is authority/Luna, not the maintainer. `isCompleteCloseEvidence` (`src/artifact/grammar.ts:2199-2201`) also drops an incomplete `CloseEvidence` child silently, so the repair must refuse incomplete evidence, not only unparsable whole XML.
**The historical-view contract is incomplete without the API.** `ChangeDurableScope` has only `carried | declared-none | absent`, and `ChangeView.observedWriteScope` is `ChangeScopeSummary | null`. `formatChangeText` (`src/query/render.ts:196-236`) dereferences `.files`/`.globs` on any truthy observed scope and `formatDurableScope` switches only over the existing durable states, and `src/query/change.test.ts:123-125` does the same with a non-null assertion. A reader that must distinguish `unavailable` from `absent` therefore forces an API change and its render/test consequences.
**The same-bundle test and documentation defects.** The real-archive T-005 guard (`src/review/core.test.ts:2036-2055`) asserts a nonzero CLI exit; the CLI exits nonzero only for displayed errors (`src/review/command.ts:118-120`), and the T-005 finding is a warning. It passes today only because three unrelated archived errors share the run, and in a warning-only physical copy it fails at `expect(result.status).not.toBe(0)`. `ngrace-plan` rule 19 also tells a planner that an archived plan's `MustExist` raises `review.confidently-wrong`; under this design it is a historical notice, so the rationale and its footprint pins move, and matching byte totals must not let the misleading paragraph survive.
**Prior-ruling overturns and counterweights.** The whole-archive malformed-refusal contract (`C-PER-BUNDLE-READERS-1-58BB7AB1`, restated by `C-ARCHIVE-CORPUS-BASELINE-2-D5F2E1C3`, tested at `src/grace-context.test.ts:455`) is overturned for the unrelated case: the slice returns its base output, the corruption stays observable through the selected reader's refusal, and a selected malformed active or archived change still refuses. The F16 counterweight (`C-REPORT-HONESTY/spec.xml:232-242`) no longer raises an error for an archived plan's missing-both-alias or foreign-id `MustExist`; the relocation and foreign-id **detection** is retained as an informational historical audit, and active plans keep the error. No version dispatcher is added and no `NGRACE_ARTIFACT_VERSION` bump is required, because no current working state becomes an error. No historical artifact byte is rewritten; scope credit is only ever taken from readable fields.

Assumptions.Assumption: Measurements re-taken 2026-10-02 on branch `feat/archive-compatibility` at HEAD `3f68a1b351efa58851f2d8245d9a8eb6ad96555b` (one policy/queue checkpoint after merged baseline `b1c925bd26789f660a75c457a44159b716b1b578`; tracked/index clean): 165 archive directories, 322 archived spec+plan roots, all `graceVersion="1.0"`; root lint 0/0; plain root review three `review.confidently-wrong` / `must-exist-missing` findings on `test-metrics.json` (keys `#0` and `#1` in `C-MINT-BASELINE-CONTROL-3-F04434E4/plan.xml`, `#0` in `C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-4-F173437E/plan.xml`). These are occupied states and expire; they are not criteria.

Independent physical-copy probes (no hardlinks, no shared writable scratch/.git) confirm the couplings and the latent defects: the three unrelated archived mutations named in `Problem` each fail lint only while present and restore to 0/0; a warning-only copy makes the real CLI review exit 0 with the T-005 warning while the unmodified repository exits 1, and the same warning-only copy fails `bun test --timeout=0 src/review/core.test.ts -t "T-005 warning remains observable"` at line 2044. The close-evaluation hole is the authority/Luna empirical probe plus the code path read; it is not re-probed here, and the unsafe hardlinked-fixture method is not repeated.
